newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand to free tapioca exports if price fixed.
newsitem.headline: Thailand to free tapioca exports if price fixed.

text.p: The Thai commerce ministry will consider scrapping its tapioca export quota to the European Union if exporters agree to buy from farmers at guaranteed prices, ministry sources said on Thursday.
"As the minister said, the ministry will remove the export quota system if exporters promise to support the guaranteed price policy to help farmers," one official said.
Tapioca exporters have been asking the government to scrap the quota system, charging that it favours selected companies, raises costs, and is open to corruption.
Thai exporters are allocated tapioca export quotas to the EU according to the size of stocks they hold and previous export performance.

Before the quota is granted, commerce ministry officials must check exporters' stocks. The system forces exporters to build up their stocks by buying more from farmers and thus support cassava roots prices.
Exporters have to pay one baht per tonne in stock checking fees.
The total tapioca export quota to the EU this year is 5.25 million tonnes.
